newsitem.title: INDIA: IMF head says "extremely positive" on India budget.
newsitem.headline: IMF head says "extremely positive" on India budget.

text.p: International Monetary Fund managing director Michel Camdessus said on Tuesday that his initial impression of India's 1997/98 (April-March) budget was extremely positive.
Asked to comment on the government's tax and spending plan which was announced last Friday, Camdessus told reporters as he arrived in the Indian capital: "My first impression is extremely positive.

"It is positive because all the people in this country, in the business community, tell me this will help them to do better and contribute better to the overall prosperity of the country," the IMF head said.
Indian stock markets have rallied since Finance Minister P. Chidambaram announced the budget, proposing corporate and personal income tax rate cuts, and lower import duties on a range of goods.
Camdessus, who was scheduled to meet Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda and Chidambaram on Wednesday, said he was in India to comment on the economy and to discuss the IMF's future role.
"I wanted to see Indian authorities and discuss with them their expectations about of the role of the IMF and in what way the IMF can later serve the world economy and your country," he said.
"This to me is very important because, contrary to what the Indians believe in general, India matters in the rest of the world, and the voice of India is of immense importance."

The IMF head praised the government's decision to press ahead with economic reforms launched in 1991 and said he was visiting India to see "the very remarkable impact" that the measures had had on the economy.
"It is very unusual for me to do that when there is not a fire to fight as I am the head of the fire brigade in the world," Camdessus said.

In 1991, India faced dwindling foreign exchange reserves and turned to the IMF for an emergency standby loan. It then began liberalising its economy, dismantling decades of socialist controls and inviting private and foreign investment.

Camdessus arrived in New Delhi from the southwestern state of Goa, where he spent two days after his weekend arrival in the southern city of Madras. He is scheduled to leave for Hong Kong late on Wednesday.
